title: Coupled quantum critical states in a circuit simulator
authors: D. B. Karki, Andrew K. Mitchell
abstract: Hybrid metal-semiconductor quantum circuits offer a controlled setting for realizing and probing strongly correlated quantum matter. A largely open question that may be addressed by such simulators is whether coupled critical states can combine into new non-Fermi liquid (NFL) phases. Inspired by the recent realization of a two-site charge-Kondo circuit [W. Pouse \textit{et al.}, \href{https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-022-01905-4}{Nat. Phys. \textbf{19}, 492 (2023)}], we uncover the fate of coupled Kondo anyons emerging from the two-channel-Kondo critical point at each site. Bosonization and quantum Brownian motion methods yield the full quasiballistic phase diagram and low-temperature transport properties, while numerical renormalization group calculations resolve the complementary weak-coupling limit. Together, these provide a unified description, and reveal robust NFL phases with continuously tunable transport and susceptibility exponents. Stronger inter-site coupling ultimately produces a screened Fermi liquid.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes coupled quantum critical states in a two-site quantum circuit simulator. Using advanced techniques like NRG and Bosonization, the authors map out the phase diagram, showing that while individual critical points persist, strong inter-site coupling ultimately drives the system into a conventional Fermi Liquid state. This work provides a detailed understanding of quantum criticality in tunable mesoscopic conductors.
main_problem: The study investigates how coupled quantum critical states, specifically those arising from the two-channel-Kondo (2CK) point, behave when subjected to inter-site coupling.
main_result: Weak coupling preserves the individual critical points, but increasing coupling drives a quantum phase transition from a Non-Fermi Liquid (NFL) state to a screened Fermi Liquid (FL) state.
method: The research employs a combination of theoretical techniques, including Bosonization, Quantum Brownian Motion, and Numerical Renormalization Group (NRG) calculations.
model_or_system: The system is a hybrid metal-semiconductor quantum circuit simulator comprising two coupled metallic islands, modeled by a Hamiltonian incorporating continuum electron spectra, tunneling (QPC), and charging energies.
key_observables:
Impurity entropy (Simp(T)), local susceptibilities ($\chi_{loc}^{s,u}(T)$), and transport/conductance exponents ($\eta, 
u$).
important_parameters: Inter-site coupling strength ($t_C$), island-lead coupling ($t$), and gate-tuned filling ($	ext{Ng}_\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on projecting the charge dynamics onto pseudospin-$ rac{1}{2}$ degrees of freedom and analyzing the system in both Kondo and quasiballistic limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the circuit schematic, NRG results showing entropy and susceptibilities, and a phase diagram mapping out different quantum regimes based on coupling ratios and gate detuning.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical circuit and Hamiltonian, applying NRG and Bosonization methods to analyze the crossover between decoupled 2CK states, intermediate NFL regimes, and the final screened FL state.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of quantum critical points and their stability under coupling is highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phases in artificial quantum materials and mesoscopic devices.
